result: On one archived 27-record response, default MCP list changed from 129881 bytes to 5102 bytes: 96.07 percent smaller. Ten summaries retain receipt IDs; offset pages cover the latest-50 window; full records remain retrievable by ID. All 71 tests pass.

limits: List now returns summaries and a first page, not all full records; compare tasks before claiming downstream efficiency.
Byte count is not tokenizer usage, billed cost or model task success.
Additional get calls can offset savings when all full records are needed.

lesson: Progressive retrieval reduces the observed discovery payload; this does not establish task accuracy, token cost or end-to-end efficiency when full records are subsequently fetched.
uncertainty: One public snapshot, deterministic replay, no models. Offset pages can shift with concurrent writes; not full database pagination.
